memory_update.content: In the reference-only international/large-cap education chunk, Pearson is the highest-priority benchmark because assessment and credentialing are closer to a chokepoint than consumer tutoring or broad professional information analytics.

RELX, EDU, and TAL should remain reference monitors rather than core underfollowed candidates unless future evidence proves material education/workforce-learning exposure, durable credential-linked demand, or a clearer supply bottleneck.
For Pearson, verify segment-level assessment, credentialing, and workforce-skills revenue, contract retention, AI content risk, and whether credential products are compliance-linked or discretionary.
For China education references EDU and TAL, verify current post-regulatory revenue mix, policy-compliant product categories, AI-learning monetization, and margin durability before any upgrade.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Assessment revenue durability, AI-related content risk, workforce credential growth, institutional contract renewal/retention, and whether credentials are compliance-linked or merely discretionary learning products.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current segment-level filings or investor materials showing assessment and workforce-skills revenue growth, margins, retention, contract duration, and AI disruption sensitivity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Pearson is the cleanest reference candidate in this chunk for assessment, credentialing, education content, and workforce-skills infrastructure. The strongest Serenity angle is not generic textbook/content recovery, but whether assessment and credentialing remain durable gateways as AI disrupts content creation and student acquisition channels.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not meaningfully underfollowed as a company. The only underfollowed angle is that investors may over-anchor on legacy textbook/content exposure and underweight assessment, testing, credentialing, and workforce-skill verification assets.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Actual education, professional-learning, medical education, or compliance-training revenue exposure versus broader analytics and information-services revenue.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment disclosures or product-level evidence proving that education/workforce-learning is material enough to influence consolidated growth, rather than being an immaterial subtheme.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: RELX has durable professional information, scientific/technical/medical content, analytics, and compliance workflow exposure that can serve as a reference benchmark for professional education and regulated knowledge infrastructure. However, its education/workforce-learning exposure is likely diluted by much larger legal, scientific, risk, and analytics businesses.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: RELX is not underfollowed. The potentially missed angle is only second-order: professional education, medical/scientific knowledge, and compliance-data workflows may sit adjacent to workforce credentialing and continuing professional learning.

ranked_candidates.company: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.
ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Current revenue mix, regulatory boundaries, overseas study demand, non-academic tutoring exposure, margin stability, and whether any products create durable credential or placement-linked outcomes.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need recent filings or earnings disclosures showing post-regulatory business mix, segment growth, margin quality, and policy-compliant product categories.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: New Oriental remains a useful international education-services reference for overseas study, consumer learning, and China policy-sensitive education demand. It ranks below Pearson and RELX because the Serenity chokepoint is less clear: demand may be real, but the supply-chain bottleneck is not obvious and regulatory boundaries can dominate fundamentals.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a high-attention China education reference, included mainly to monitor policy-risk recovery and international education demand rather than to identify a hidden supply-chain node.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Regulatory constraints, current product mix, AI learning monetization, profitability, retention, and whether AI tools improve measurable learning outcomes or merely create product novelty.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need recent company disclosures proving policy-compliant revenue growth, AI product monetization, retention, margins, and reduced regulatory downside.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: TAL is relevant as a high-beta reference for consumer learning, China education regulation, and AI-learning product monetization, but it is the weakest Serenity candidate in this chunk because the bottleneck is unclear and evidence for durable AI-learning economics is not yet established in the provided context.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a widely watched China education/AI-learning name, so it does not meet the underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery lens.

summary: This candidate chunk contains only large-cap/high-attention reference names, so the Serenity priority is mostly contextual rather than underfollowed alpha discovery. Pearson ranks first because assessment, credentialing, and workforce-skills infrastructure are more directly tied to durable education chokepoints than the broader businesses of RELX or the policy-sensitive Chinese tutoring platforms. RELX is useful as a second-order professional information and compliance-learning reference, but education purity is weak. New Oriental and TAL are lower priority because their theme signal is heavily mixed with consumer demand, China policy risk, and uncertain monetization of new learning products. No company in this chunk receives a high underfollowed_discovery score because all are large/high-attention reference names rather than obscure small/mid-cap chokepoint candidates.
